name: Al-Muthaqqib al-Abdi
bio: Al-A'idh ibn Mihsan was a pre-Islamic poet of Abd al-Qays from Bahrayn, the region of eastern Arabia. He knew the court at al-Hira and praised Amr ibn Hind and al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir. His sobriquet al-Muthaqqib, “the piercer”, is traditionally traced to the women who pierce peepholes in their travelling curtains in one of his poems. Al-Mufaddal preserved his verse on a much-travelled camel and on the terms of friendship. Al-Zirikli dates his death to around thirty-five years before the Hijra (about 588 CE).
